title: RxJS Deep Dive: Stream Signature Reference
attribution: These definitions and teaching notes were created with the help of GPT-6 Astra, under the course direction of Hans Schenker.
notationSummary: Cω-inspired stream shorthand that translates into ordinary TypeScript types. It is explanatory notation, not syntax accepted by the TypeScript compiler.
legend: A, B
Input and output payload types. S is accumulated state; K is a key; O is an opening-signal payload; R is a registration token; D is a default-value type.
A*
Observable<A>: a stream with zero or more next values per subscription. The type does not promise values, completion, a clock, or shared execution.
Optional occurrence refinements: zero or one / exactly one / one or more next values. State the lifetime and termination assumptions. Ordinary Observable<A> does not enforce these bounds.
An array value / an Observable whose next values are arrays.
A tuple of two sources / a stream of two-value tuples.
An outer stream whose next values are inner streams.
A => B
A value function; in TypeScript write (value: A) => B.
A source-to-result transformation; in TypeScript write (source: Observable<A>) => Observable<B>.
Input<A>
ObservableInput<A>: Observable, promise-like, iterable, async iterable, array-like, interoperable Observable, or readable-stream-like input.
A stream whose next values can belong to either payload type.
A & B
A value satisfying both structural requirements; used for a group stream with a key property.
never*
No next payload values. Completion, error, or remaining open must be described separately.
Notice<A>
ObservableNotification<A>: { kind: "N"; value: A } | { kind: "E"; error: unknown } | { kind: "C" }.
param?: Type
An optional configuration parameter. This question mark is parameter syntax, not the stream-cardinality suffix.
globalNotes: The cards show selected common forms. Callback indices, some optional parameters, and the exhaustive overload sets live in the linked API and pinned source.
Creation functions return Observables directly. Most pipeable functions return transformations used by pipe; partition and connectable forms have explicitly different result shapes.
Unless a card says otherwise, next, error, complete, and unsubscription are separate concerns. Unsubscription is not a complete notification.

Examples omit imports and generally show Observable expressions, not subscribe calls. Their next/complete comments describe a subscription allowed to finish; external-request outcomes remain conditional.
Durations normally use milliseconds with asyncScheduler. A supplied scheduler can provide a different or virtual clock. Integer counts and positive concurrency limits are the teaching defaults.
null and undefined are ordinary emitted values. of(undefined) emits once; EMPTY emits no next values.
An operator factory builds a description. Work starts through subscription, although argument expressions and eager input creation may already have run.
Shorthand describes type shape. Read the adjacent behavior policy and execution details before claiming two operators are equivalent.

categoryIntros.Creation Operators: Start from values, callbacks, events, requests, or a clock. Read when work begins and how the subscription ends.
categoryIntros.Join Creation Operators: Supply all sources directly. Tuple joins preserve positions; union joins forward values from different sources.
categoryIntros.Transformation Operators: Change payloads, accumulate state, group values, or choose an Action Policy for inner subscriptions.
categoryIntros.Filtering Operators: Choose which values pass. Similar A* => A* shapes can have very different gates, deadlines, and completion rules.
categoryIntros.Join Operators: Combine a primary source with companions, or flatten an outer stream. Read who triggers output and when inner subscriptions start.
categoryIntros.Multicasting Operators: Choose how listeners share source connections and what later listeners receive. Type shape alone does not specify this policy.
categoryIntros.Error Handling Operators: Choose whether an error terminates, selects another input, or requests another subscription.
categoryIntros.Utility Operators: Observe execution, schedule work or delivery, measure time, enforce deadlines, or convert notifications.
categoryIntros.Conditional and Boolean Operators: Answer questions about a subscription. Many answers require completion; a counterexample can sometimes end the search early.
categoryIntros.Mathematical and Aggregate Operators: Produce a final aggregate when the source completes. Compare with scan when learners need every intermediate state.

glossary: SchedulerLike
A scheduler supplies now() and scheduling operations. It can represent real or virtual time; choosing one does not imply another thread.
TimestampProvider
A clock object with now(): number. It measures time and need not schedule work.
ThrottleConfig
An object with optional leading and trailing booleans. Defaults: leading true, trailing false.
RetryConfig / RepeatConfig
Retry uses count?, delay?, resetOnSuccess?; repeat uses count? and delay?. Retry count means retries after the original run; repeat count means total runs.
ShareConfig<A>
Selects a connector and resetOnError, resetOnComplete, and resetOnRefCountZero policies. Each reset can be a boolean or a callback returning a reset notifier.
ShareReplayConfig
Requires refCount in the typed object form; bufferSize, windowTime, and scheduler are optional. Prefer explicit bounded buffering and an explicit refCount decision.
ConnectConfig<A>
A selector-sharing configuration with a required connector factory returning a SubjectLike<A>.
ConnectableConfig<A>

An explicit-connection configuration with a required connector when an object is supplied, and optional resetOnDisconnect. This name comes from the implementation; it is not a root-exported RxJS 7.8.2 type.
Connectable<A>
An Observable<A> that also exposes connect(): Subscription. The modern connectable() factory returns this shape.
ConnectableObservable<A>
The legacy connectable class shape, carrying older connection and refCount machinery. It is distinct from the minimal modern Connectable<A> interface.
Subject<A> / SubjectLike<A>

A Subject can receive next/error/complete and be subscribed to as an Observable. SubjectLike names the structural observer-and-subscribable contract. Its subtype determines replay and terminal behavior.
Observer<A> / Subscription / Unsubscribable
An Observer handles next/error/complete. A Subscription manages teardown. Unsubscribable is the smaller contract with unsubscribe(): void.
GroupedObservable<K, A>
An Observable<A> with a key: K property. The shorthand (A* & { readonly key: K }) preserves both stream shape and the group key.
TimeoutConfig<A, B*> / TimeoutInfo<A>
TimeoutConfig names first?, each?, scheduler?, with?, and meta?. TimeoutInfo carries meta, seen, and lastValue. The shorthand specializes its fallback ObservableInput parameter to B*.
Notice<A>
The structural N/E/C notification union defined in the legend. materialize returns Notification instances compatible with that union; dematerialize accepts the structural union.
AjaxConfig / AjaxResponse<A>
AjaxConfig chooses the XMLHttpRequest request and progress options. AjaxResponse<A> is the wrapper whose response field contains A; selecting a type does not validate a server response.
WebSocketSubjectConfig<A> / WebSocketSubject<A>
The config supplies connection, serialization, and deserialization options. The result is both a stream of received A values and an outgoing next(value) interface.
EventTarget / AddEventListenerOptions
The selected DOM event target and its capture, once, and passive listener options. fromEvent also supports other event-source protocols.
Request / RequestInit / Response
The platform fetch request, request-options, and response types. The response body is consumed separately unless the fromFetch selector includes it.
Date
A JavaScript absolute date value, interpreted by the relevant operator against its supplied clock.
Record<string, A> / A[K] / keyof A
A string-keyed record; the value type at property K; and the permitted property-key types of A. Known-property shorthand assumes K extends keyof A.
Exclude<A, B> / readonly
Exclude removes union members assignable to B; readonly forbids assignment through that property in TypeScript. Neither performs runtime validation.
